The Reducing Medically Unnecessary Delays in Care Act (H.R. 2433) already mandates physician-led prior authorization decisions under Medicare - a critical safeguard against insurance bureaucrats denying care. While limiting annual authorization requirements sounds patient-friendly, Section 3(1) reveals the loophole: insurers can still impose endless "medical necessity" reviews through their own clinical criteria.

The Autoimmune Association's own data shows 73% of denied claims get approved on appeal - proof these reviews exist to slow-roll care, not protect patients. Real reform would ban prior authorization entirely for chronic conditions requiring stable therapies.

This bill lets insurers keep their denial factories running while pretending to streamline bureaucracy. Until Congress forces CMMI to audit every MA plan's approval rates and ties Medicare reimbursements to denial ratios, these performative "reforms" just repackage the same waste.
